evidence: The original attachPaneSinkViaEmitter registered `client.on("output", onOutput)` listeners, so a sink attached inside an output handler joined the live emitter Set and an earlier throwing listener aborted sink delivery, unlike TmuxClient's snapshot-before-emit path. dcd964c extracted PaneSinkRegistry and every client now calls `paneSinks.dispatch(msg)` before emit, which is the dispatch point the reviewer asked for.
guidance_note: When a new adapter claims to be behaviorally identical to an existing implementation, extract and reuse that implementation instead of rebuilding it on a weaker path, and test the claimed invariants (no back-fill, throw isolation) on the adapter itself.

evidence: The comment still said pre-bound handlers keep the "[HOT-PATH] byte callback" closure-free, but bytes had moved to attachPaneSink and only reconnected/subscription-changed/activity handlers remained; dcd964c rewrote the comment to name those handlers and point at the paneSink write closure.
guidance_note: When moving a code path off an API, grep the touched file for comments describing the old path (here "[HOT-PATH]" and "off()") and rewrite them in the same commit.

evidence: The disposer's `const set = this.attachments.get(paneId)` holds a Map<symbol, PaneByteSink>; 985fcec renamed it to perPaneNow. The flag is a false positive for causation: this disposer was moved byte-for-byte from TmuxClient.attachPaneSink (`const set = this.paneSinks.get(paneId)` in the removed lines of dcd964c), so the misnomer predates review.

The "not the live Set" and "per-pane Set's *iteration order*" comments are new text in dcd964c's PaneSinkRegistry (TmuxClient's original said "mutations to `paneSinks`"), and attachments is a Map. 985fcec reworded both to "per-pane attachments", and dropping the type name from a why-comment is a fair use of the cited law.
guidance_note: Before pushing a fix that writes new prose around a data structure, check every noun in the new comments against the declared types in the same file.

evidence: 985fcec fixed the two "Set" mentions F4 pointed at but left "not the live attachment Set" in the PaneDispatchSnapshot JSDoc, also written in dcd964c; ae9894b fixed that one, and the agent calls it the "last lingering" reference.
guidance_note: When a finding flags a wrong term in some places, grep the whole file for the term and fix every hit before pushing, not just the cited lines.

evidence: The new test header in dcd964c claimed the registry promises "no throw-poisoning across sinks attached at dispatch time", but dispatch() has no try/catch and the PaneByteSink contract puts cross-sink error isolation out of scope. The agent conceded ("I conflated two different properties") and ae9894b rewrote the header, so the pushback reply-hint is misleading.
guidance_note: When writing a test-file header that lists what the code under test promises, check each listed property against a test in the file or a line in the implementation, and drop any that has neither.

evidence: dcd964c's new test said "`a` attaches a SIBLING sink mid-dispatch", but `trigger.write` calls `reg.attach(1, lateAttached)`. The flagged commit ae9894b did not touch this comment; it came from the F1 fix that created the test file and was only noticed in round 3. dbdfc11 names `trigger`.
guidance_note: When writing a test comment that names which object performs an action, check that object's name against the code in the test body.

evidence: The PR description still advertised attachPaneSinkViaEmitter, which dcd964c deleted in answer to F1; the agent rewrote the description. Calling a stale PR body a one-source-of-truth violation stretches the law: the body is a description that went stale, not a second copy of state the code reads.
guidance_note: When a fix deletes or replaces a public symbol the PR description names, rewrite the description's surface section in the same push as the fix.

narrative: Round 0's F1 was a real semantic bug: the emitter-backed adapter did not match TmuxClient's snapshot and throw-isolation guarantees. The agent fixed it properly by extracting PaneSinkRegistry. That fix brought in a new file of comments and a new test file, and rounds 1-4 were spent on prose in that new code: Set/Map terminology fixed in two passes, a test header that overclaimed throw isolation, a test comment naming the wrong actor, and a stale PR description. F3 is the one later finding not caused by the fix; it is relocated code.
guidance_observations: A large structural fix that writes new comments and a new test file got its prose reviewed one nit per round; reading every new comment against the code before pushing would have collapsed rounds 2-4.
The terminology fix in 985fcec covered only the lines the reviewer quoted, so the same term came back the next round.

evidence: The hunk shows `[LAW:one-type-per-` / `behavior]` wrapped across two comment lines, which a grep for the token cannot match; 99b9b72 moved the full token onto one line.
guidance_note: When rewrapping a comment that contains a [LAW:token] marker, start the marker on its own line so the formatter never splits the token.

evidence: The original test read `dist/client.d.ts` and threw "Run 'pnpm run build' before this test", so `pnpm test` on a clean checkout fails. Scanning the source .ts files (99b9b72) removes the build dependency, and because tsc copies JSDoc into .d.ts unchanged, a source check is a sound stand-in for this assertion. The locality-or-seam citation decorates a cost argument rather than naming a seam.
guidance_note: Before adding a test that reads build output, run the test suite from a clean checkout; if it needs a build, assert on the source the build is derived from.

evidence: The original regex `\b(?:event|type)\s*:\s*"output"` ignored the `method` argument, which made the on/off loop redundant, and it was tied to the parameter names event/type. 99b9b72 anchored on `(?:on|off)\s*\(\s*\w+`, and the agent correctly points out that this also stops matching `dispatch({ type: "output" })` object literals.
guidance_note: When a helper takes a parameter like `method`, confirm the parameter actually narrows the matching logic; if it does not, it is an unused input that hides a gap.

evidence: 99b9b72 switched the test from `.d.ts` to source scanning, but the PR body still said it "walks each emitted .d.ts". The agent admits "I missed updating the PR body".
guidance_note: When a review fix changes the approach the PR description explains, edit the description in the same push.

evidence: The docstring line "`/** … *‍/` JSDoc block", with an invisible joiner inside the terminator, is a + line in 99b9b72, the fix that rewrote expectAllOverloadsDeprecated for F3. 4e9d4d1 removed it, and the agent verified with `grep -P '\x{200D}'`.
guidance_note: Never write a block-comment terminator inside a block comment; describe it in words instead of hiding it with an invisible character.

evidence: `source.lastIndexOf("/**", sigStart)` can walk past an overload that has no JSDoc and pick up the previous overload's @deprecated block, which gives a false pass. 4e9d4d1 added a whitespace-only gap check, and the agent tested it on a synthetic missing-JSDoc case. The flag is a false positive for causation: the same lastIndexOf walk-back ("Walk back to the nearest /** opener") was in the round-0 code, and 99b9b72 only carried it over.
guidance_note: When a test looks up "the nearest preceding X" to attribute X to a target, assert X is adjacent to the target, or the test will credit a neighbor's X.

evidence: The published @deprecated JSDoc pointed consumers at "`src/pane-sink.ts` and the built-in sinks in `src/sinks/`", paths that do not exist in an installed package. The flag is a false positive: this text is from the original commit, and the named commit 99b9b72 did not touch src/client.ts. 4e9d4d1 named the exported symbols and their subpaths instead.
guidance_note: In JSDoc that ships in .d.ts, refer to exported symbol names and package subpaths, never to in-repo source paths.

evidence: The agent checked that pane-terminal's package.json exports only subpaths, so the IMPL.md text "`XtermSink` in `@promptctl/pane-terminal`" named an import path that does not exist. The flag is a false positive: the IMPL.md text came from the original commit, and 99b9b72 did not touch IMPL.md.
guidance_note: When docs name an import location, check it against the package.json `exports` map before writing it.

evidence: The header comment `grep -n "[LAW:" src/` was added in 99b9b72 as part of the F2 rewrite. An unescaped `[` opens a bracket expression, so the command errors or matches the wrong lines and does not find markers. 7cf9cae escaped it; the agent's own F1 reply had used the same broken pattern.
guidance_note: Run any shell command you put in a comment once before committing it.

evidence: "forbids the `Uint8Array → string` misdecode" overclaims, because a custom PaneByteSink still gets raw bytes and can decode them however it likes; 123cef5 narrowed the claim to the built-in sinks. The flag is a false positive for causation: "forbids" is in the original JSDoc (round-0 hunk), and 0c7b228 only reformatted the overload signatures.
guidance_note: When writing a guarantee into public docs, phrase it as what the API enforces; a property that depends on which sink the caller chooses gets a conditional.

narrative: This JSDoc-deprecation PR had three real round-0 findings. The fix for F2/F3 rewrote the test to scan source, and that rewrite left the PR description out of date, added a hidden-Unicode terminator, and put a broken grep example in the header. Round 1's F6-F8 flags are false positives for causation: the lastIndexOf walk-back and the src/ path references predate review. F10 was a pre-existing overclaim the reviewer only spotted in round 4, after a clean round 3.
guidance_observations: The test rewrite added new prose (header, docstring, a command example) without checking it, and each slip cost a finding.
The reviewer is nondeterministic: round 3 came back clean, and round 4 then found a pre-existing overclaim after a formatting-only commit.

evidence: With `msg is M & PaneOutputMessage`, a `{type:"output"}` value with no paneId/data narrows to PaneOutputMessage. 3d9357e's `Extract<M, PaneOutputMessage>` keeps only the union members that really are PaneOutputMessage, so an incompatible input narrows to never. That keeps the else-branch narrowing the reviewer wanted to preserve, without overloads.
guidance_note: When widening a type predicate to a generic input, narrow with Extract<M, Target> rather than M & Target, so the predicate never fabricates fields the runtime check does not inspect.

evidence: asPaneOutput had the same `M & PaneOutputMessage` unsoundness; 3d9357e changed it to `Extract<M, PaneOutputMessage> | null`. The reply's claim that a misused input "returns null" is wrong at runtime: `asPaneOutput({type:'output'})` still returns the object, typed as null. That type lie only affects misuse inputs, so the choice of fix is still defensible.
guidance_note: When a fix changes a predicate's return type, describe what the function returns at runtime for a misuse input, not only what the type says.

evidence: The comment called `attachAllPanesSink` a sole writer of the registry, but the registry method is `attachAllPanes` (the *Sink name is TmuxClient's public wrapper); d4297b7 corrected it. The flag is a false positive: 3d9357e touched only fake-tmux-client.ts and protocol/types.ts, so this pane-sink.ts comment is from the original commit.
guidance_note: When an invariant comment lists the methods that are allowed to write state, copy the method names from the class they are on.

evidence: PaneByteMultiplexer and attachAllPanes are a new public surface with a new dispatch path (fan-out with no per-pane sinks), and the PR deleted tests without adding any for it. d4297b7 added seven contract-level tests. The flag is a false positive: the surface is from the original commit, not 3d9357e.
guidance_note: When a PR adds a public surface and deletes the tests of the surface it replaces, write tests for the new contract (delivery, snapshot, end-on-dispose) in the same PR.

evidence: The contract said a throwing multiplexer "poisons the chunk's dispatch frame for sinks attached after it", but dispatch runs per-pane sinks before multiplexers, so a multiplexer throw can only skip later multiplexers; 098b6af fixed the doc. The flag is a false positive: 14ffa0d changed computeSnapshot, not this doc. Citing single-enforcer to justify iteration order is a decoration.
guidance_note: When documenting the blast radius of a throw, trace the actual loop order in dispatch and describe that order.

evidence: The JSDoc said "one parsed `PaneOutputMessage`", but `dispatch(msg: TmuxMessage)` early-returns on non-byte messages, so the doc did not match the signature. The agent kept the signature so the isPaneOutput discriminator stays in one place, which is a real single-enforcer reason, and fixed the doc in 098b6af. The flag is a false positive: the JSDoc came from the original commit, not 14ffa0d.
guidance_note: When a method's JSDoc names an input type, check it against the parameter's declared type.

narrative: This PR removed pane bytes from the emitter type surface. Round 0 found a real type-predicate soundness hole, and the agent fixed it with Extract rather than the overloads the reviewer proposed, which was the better fix. The rest of the findings are pre-existing doc and test gaps in the original multiplexer code. The flags on 3d9357e and 14ffa0d are false positives because neither commit touched the flagged text. Round 2 was a reviewer error, not a review.
guidance_observations: The new multiplexer surface shipped with docs that misdescribed its own dispatch order and input type; reading the docs against the dispatch loop before opening the PR would have caught F5 and F6.
The PR deleted tests for the old path without adding any for the new public surface.

evidence: The design doc says "shared per-pane `TextDecoder({ stream: true })`", but `stream` is an option to `decode()`, not to the constructor. The thread is unresolved with no reply, and the PR is still open.
guidance_note: When a design doc sketches a platform API, write the actual call shape (here `new TextDecoder()` plus `decode(chunk, { stream: true })`) instead of a remembered approximation.

evidence: The reviewer says protocol/types.ts types `SessionChangedMessage.sessionId` and `WindowAddMessage.windowId` as number, while the doc's PaneScope uses string. The packet does not include protocol/types.ts, so the mismatch cannot be confirmed. No reply.
guidance_note: When a design doc names identifier types, copy them from the existing protocol types, or state that the type is changing.

evidence: The hunk shows "On detach, any buffered text in the line splitter is flushed as a final `onLine` call". The later lifecycle section the reviewer says contradicts it (flush only when the last admitting attachment detaches) is not in the packet. No reply.

PRs #55 and #57 show the existing class is PaneSinkRegistry in src/pane-sink.ts, while this doc calls the component `SinkRegistry` and gives no note on the rename. That is a real but minor clarity gap, since a design that supersedes a component may rename it. No reply.
guidance_note: When a design doc renames an existing component, say which current class it replaces.

evidence: `type PaneMeta = { sessionId: string; windowId: string }` has the same string-versus-number question as F2. The packet does not show the protocol types it would have to match. No reply.
The LinePipeline sketch repeats `decoder: TextDecoder({ stream: true })`, the same constructor misuse as F1, and the doc has no flush call on teardown. No reply on an open PR.
guidance_note: When fixing a mistaken API shape in one place in a doc, search the doc for every repeat of it.

narrative: This is an open design-doc PR with one review round and six unanswered findings. Two are confirmed errors in how the doc describes the TextDecoder API, one is a naming clarity gap, and three depend on protocol types or doc sections the packet does not show. The packet's diff stats (+24471 in 180 files, 49 commits) are much larger than the single design doc the reviewer summarized, which suggests the branch carries much more than the doc.
guidance_observations: The agent never addressed this review; all six threads have no reply.
The design doc restates current-code identifiers and platform APIs from memory instead of checking them against the code.
